Even `timeout -s KILL 30` didn't kill it within the 180s tool limit! That's bizarre. Unless the tool's timeout measurement counts differently... The tool reported "Command exceeded 180 seconds" but the inner timeout was 30s. So `time` + `timeout` should have finished in 30s.

Unless... the process is unkillable? Or the tool's output capture is hanging because the child inherited the stdout pipe and holds it open! Yes — that's it: `timeout` kills the python process, but if the planner spawned... no. Hmm.

Actually wait. Maybe the planner process isn't killed because `timeout -s KILL 30` sends SIGKILL to the direct child (python3). Then python3 dies. But the output pipe stays open if a grandchild holds it. There are no grandchildren... unless OpenBLAS spawns threads (they don't hold the pipe).

Hmm, let me reconsider: maybe the issue is that the *bash* tool wraps the command and waits for all processes to exit / for the pipe to close.

Let me test with output redirected to a file instead of a pipe, to avoid pipe-related hangs.

arguments.command: cd /app/work && (time timeout -s KILL 30 python3 /app/submission/planner.py < oneshot.jsonl > out.txt 2> err.txt) > timed.txt 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; cat timed.txt; echo "--- out:"; head -c 300 out.txt; echo; echo "--- err:"; head -c 500 err.txt
